\begin{lemma}[Finite-class counting]\label{compression:counting}
Let $W\subseteq Z$ be a Borel $\mathcal U$-invariant set all of whose
$\mathcal U$-classes are finite.  If $B\subseteq W$ is Borel and meets
each such class exactly once, then
\[
 \lambda(B)=\kappa(\mathcal U;W).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Small complete sets]\label{compression:complete-set}
For every Borel subrelation $\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal R$ and every
$\varepsilon>0$, there is a Borel $\mathcal T$-complete set
$M\subseteq Z$ such that
\[
 \lambda(M)\leq\kappa(\mathcal T)+\varepsilon.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Compression]\label{compression:main}\label{compression:lemma}
On the finite-measure space $(Z,\lambda)$ with the ambient relation
$\mathcal R$ described above, suppose
$\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal Q\subseteq
\mathcal R$ are Borel equivalence relations and
$\mathcal Q=\mathcal S\vee\mathcal E$, where $\mathcal E$ is a
countable family of measure-preserving Borel partial isomorphisms with
finite total cost.  For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a countable
family $\mathcal F$ of measure-preserving Borel partial isomorphisms
inside $\mathcal Q$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{compression:bound}
 \mathcal Q=\mathcal T\vee\mathcal F,
 \qquad
 C(\mathcal F)\leq C(\mathcal E)-\kappa(\mathcal S)
                          +\kappa(\mathcal T)+\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{deployment:main}
Let $\Gamma=A*_J B$ be finitely generated, let $J$ be infinite, and
let $\Gamma$ act essentially freely and p.m.p. on a standard probability
space $(X,\mu)$. If $\delta_X$ is the infimum cost of graphings that
generate $\mathcal R_A$ together with the supplied relation
$\mathcal R_J$, then
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_\Gamma)\geq 1+\delta_X.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{intro:main}
Put $K=e^{96}96^{99}/95^{95}$, choose
\[
 0<\alpha<1/200,\qquad K\alpha^3<1/2,
 \qquad \eta=\alpha/100.
\]
For the group and actions just defined,
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright X})
      \ge1+\eta,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright Y_M})
      \le1+\frac{99}{M}\quad(M>100).
\]
In particular, choosing an integer $M>\max\{100,99/\eta\}$ gives
two essentially free p.m.p. actions of the same finitely generated
group with strictly different costs. Thus the general fixed-price
assertion is false.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Planar word lemma]
\label{planar:main}
Let $H$ be generated by a finite alphabet $S$, let $U$ be a disjoint
finite alphabet, and put $L=H*F(U)$. Let $\mathcal R$ be a family of
words in $L$ with the following properties.
Each $r\in\mathcal R$ has $m(r)\geq 7$ exterior occurrences, all positive
and with pairwise distinct underlying generators.  Distinct relators
share at most one generator from $U$.  Suppose that the natural map
\[
 H\longrightarrow D
 :=L/\langle\!\langle\mathcal R\rangle\!\rangle
\]
is injective.  If a cyclically $H$-reduced word $W$ has an exterior
occurrence and represents $1$ in $D$, then at least one of the following
conclusions holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W$ has a full cyclic match with a relator or its inverse;
\item $W$ has two intervals disjoint in their exterior occurrences, each
  matching an interval of a cyclic relator or its inverse with at least
  $m(r)-3$ exterior occurrences, where $r$ is the relator matched by that
  interval.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{rank:main}
Let $V$ and $\mathcal T$ be sets of cardinality $n$.  For each
$t\in\mathcal T$, let
\[
 r_t=x_{c(t,0)}x_{c(t,1)}\cdots x_{c(t,99)},\qquad c(t,i)\in V,
 \qquad
 D=\langle x_v\ (v\in V)\mid r_t=1\ (t\in\mathcal T)\rangle.
\]
For $T\subseteq\mathcal T$, put
$N(T)=\{c(t,i):t\in T,\ 0\le i\le99\}$.
Call a row $t$ bad if it has a repeated column, or if it shares at least
two distinct columns with another row, and let $b$ be the number of bad
rows.  Suppose that
\[
 0<\alpha<\frac1{200},\qquad \alpha n\ge1,
 \qquad 100b\le\alpha n,
\]
and that
\begin{equation}\label{rank:expansion}
 |N(T)|>96|T|\qquad
 \text{whenever }1\le |T|\le\alpha n.
\end{equation}
Then the minimum size of a generating set of $D$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{rk}(D)>\frac{\alpha n}{100}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{rank:asymptotic}
Suppose that a sequence of length-$100$ row systems satisfies
\eqref{rank:expansion} for a fixed $0<\alpha<1/200$, their sizes
$n$ tend to infinity, and their bad-row counts satisfy $b=o(n)$.
Then their presented groups satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{rk}(D)>\frac{\alpha n}{100}
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n,
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{rk}(D)}n
 \ge\frac\alpha{100}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are a separable complex Hilbert space $H$
and unital, norm-separable $C^*$-algebras $A,B\subseteq\B(H)$ with common
identity $\id_H$ such that
\[
\KK(A,B)<\varepsilon,\qquad A''=B'',
\]
but no unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfies $uAu^*=B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:invariant}
Let $P,Q\subseteq D\subseteq\B(L)$ be unital $C^*$-algebras.
The identity in Definition~\ref{def:tensor} is preserved by conjugating
$P$ with any unitary normalizing $D$. If $(U_n)$ is a sequence of unitaries
in $\B(L)$ satisfying $U_nDU_n^*=D$ and every $b\in Q$ admits the
approximation \eqref{eq:pointwise-normalizers}, then the identity for $P$
implies the identity for $Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:obstruction}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:sequences}, suppose that
$P$ has the spatial tensor-norm identity relative to $D$, whereas $Q$
does not. Then $\E_D(P)$ and $\E_D(Q)$ are not spatially conjugate.
If $W\in\B(L)$ is unitary and $WPW^*=Q$, then nevertheless
\[
\KK(\E_D(P),\E_D(Q))\le2\norm{W-\id_L}.
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:dimensiondrop}
Let $B$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra, let $p\ge2$, and suppose that a
\cpc order-zero map $\alpha:M_p\to B$ and $s\in B$ satisfy
\[
 h=\alpha(1),\qquad s^*s=1-h,\qquad \alpha(e_{11})s=s.
\]
There is a unital homomorphism
$I(p,p+1)\to B$ whose range contains $\alpha(M_p)$ and $s$.
Consequently $F_\omega(A)$ receives a unital homomorphism from
$I(p,p+1)$ for every $p\ge2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous domination for weighted inclusions]
\label{cen:weighted-domination}
Let $D\subseteq E$ be a nuclear $C^*$-subalgebra of a $C^*$-algebra
$E$, and let $v,w$ be positive contractions in $\widetilde E\cap D'$.
Put $\Phi(a)=va$ and $\Psi(a)=wa$ for $a\in D$; these products
belong to $E$. Suppose that
\[
 \Phi(a)\in\Ideal_E(\Psi(a))\qquad(a\in D_+).
\]
Then for every finite set $F\subset D$ and every $\delta>0$, there
are an integer $N\ge1$ and $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in E$ such that
\[
 \left\|va-\sum_{j=1}^N v_j^*wa v_j\right\|<\delta
 \qquad(a\in F).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Coordinate ideal visibility]\label{prop:idealvisibility}
For every fixed $k\ge2$ there is a \cpc order-zero map
$\nu:M_k\to A_\omega\cap A'$, represented by \cpc maps
$\nu_n:M_k\to A$, with weights $h_n^\nu=\nu_n(1)$, such that the
following holds.  For every test $(a,\eps)$, put
\[
 b=(a-\eps/8)_+,\qquad
 y_n^\nu=a^{1/2}g(h_n^\nu)^2a^{1/2}.
\]
There are integers $L_{a,\eps,n}\ge1$ and an $\omega$-large set
$E_{a,\eps}$ on which
\begin{equation}\label{cmp:I}
 [b]\le L_{a,\eps,n}[(y_n^\nu-\eps/20)_+]
          \quad\text{in }\Cu(A).
\end{equation}
The integers need not be bounded as $n$ varies.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Uniform approximation from below]
\label{prop:unital-approx}
Let $A$ be a unital simple infinite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra with
nonempty tracial state space $T(A)$. For every $p\in A_+$ and
$\eta>0$, there are a finite integer $L$ and $w\in M_L(A)_+$
such that
\[
 0\le\tau(p)-d_\tau(w)\le\eta
 \qquad(\tau\in T(A)),
\]
where matrix traces are unnormalized. No exactness, nuclearity, or
comparison assumption is required.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Small nonzero classes]
\label{ext:lem:small}
If $A$ is simple and non-elementary, then $B=A\otimes\K$ is simple
and has no minimal projections. For every nonzero $e\in B_+$ and
integer $M\ge1$, there is a nonzero $h\in B_+$ with
\[
 M[h]\le[e].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Functional trichotomy]
\label{ext:lem:trichotomy}
Let $A$ be simple and nonzero. Every functional on $\Cu(A)$ is
either zero, infinite on every nonzero class, or positive on every
nonzero class and finite on every class $[(c-\delta)_+]$ with
$c\in(A\otimes\K)_+$ and $\delta>0$.
The third type consists exactly of the functionals finite and
positive at some class.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Absorption from condition \textup{(C)}]
\label{thm:condition-C}
Let $A$ be a nonzero separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra satisfying
\textup{(C)}. For every fixed free ultrafilter $\omega$ on
$\mathbb N$, there is a unital $*$-homomorphism
$\Z\to F_\omega(A)$. Consequently $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[The canonical Cuntz-semigroup map]
\label{cor:canonical}
Let $A$ be a separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra, and let
$\iota:A\to A\otimes_{\min}\Z$ be $\iota(a)=a\otimes1_\Z$.
If $\Cu(\iota):\Cu(A)\to\Cu(A\otimes_{\min}\Z)$ is an
isomorphism, then $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[An abstract Cuntz-semigroup criterion]
\label{cor:abstract-cu}
Let $A$ be a separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra. Then
\[
 A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Cu(A)\cong\Cu(A\otimes_{\min}\Z)
 \text{ in the category }\mathbf{Cu}.
\]
The isomorphism on the right is abstract: it is not required to be
induced by the first-factor embedding, or by any $*$-homomorphism.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[The relative trace ideal]\label{loc:sigma-ideal}
Definition~\ref{loc:relative-ideal} is independent of the bounded
representative.  It defines a closed two-sided ideal of $A_\omega$.
Moreover, for every separable $C^*$-subalgebra $C_0\subseteq A_\omega$
there is a positive contraction $e\in J_b\cap C_0'$ such that
$ey=y$ for every $y\in J_b\cap C_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Localized norm-central trace filling]
\label{prop:localized-trace}
Let $k\ge2$, $b\in A_+$, and let $a\in\Ideal_A(b)$ be a positive
contraction.  Suppose that, for some finite $C>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{loc:relative-rank}
 d_\tau(a)\le C d_\tau(b)\qquad\text{for every }\tau.
\end{equation}
There is a \cpc order-zero map $\phi:M_k\to A_\omega\cap A'$ with
weight $h$ such that every positive contractive representative
$(h_n)$ of $h$ has the following property: for every $\eta>0$, on a
common $\omega$-large set of coordinates,
\begin{equation}\label{loc:TL}
 \tau\bigl(a^{1/2}(1-h_n)a^{1/2}\bigr)
       \le\eta d_\tau(b)
 \qquad(d_\tau(b)<\infty).
\end{equation}
In particular the left side is exactly zero when $d_\tau(b)=0$.

The finite-coordinate form permits arbitrary relative trace accuracies
together with prescribed finite norm tests. Given a
finite set $F\subset A$, finitely many pairs $(a_l,b_l)$ satisfying
\eqref{loc:relative-rank} with finite constants $C_l$, positive
accuracies $\eta_l$, and $\rho>0$, there is a \cpc map
$\theta:M_k\to A$ whose matrix-unit order-zero defects and
commutators with $F$ have norm less than $\rho$, and whose weight
satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{loc:TL-coordinate}
 \tau\bigl(a_l^{1/2}(1-\theta(1))a_l^{1/2}\bigr)
     \le\eta_l d_\tau(b_l)
 \qquad(d_\tau(b_l)<\infty)
\end{equation}
for every $l$, simultaneously over all the indicated traces.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:norm}
Suppose that \(A\) is separable and satisfies \textup{(C)}.  For every positive contraction \(x\in A\), every
\(\gamma>0\), and every integer \(k\ge2\), there are \cpc maps
\(\nu_n:M_k\to A\) such that
\[
 \nu:M_k\longrightarrow \Aomega\cap A',
 \qquad \nu(z)=[(\nu_n(z))_n],
\]
is order zero, and there is a number \(\kappa>0\) for which
\begin{equation}\label{norm:coordinate-visibility}
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{for every }n\in\N\text{ and every irreducible representation }\sigma
 \text{ of }A,\\
 \|\sigma(x)\|\ge\gamma
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \|\sigma(x\nu_n(1))\|\ge\kappa .
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
One may take \(\kappa=\gamma^2/32\).  In particular, the estimate holds on
one \(\omega\)-large set of coordinates simultaneously for every
irreducible representation, including representations chosen separately
at each coordinate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}\label{norm:finite-cover}
Let \(x\in A_+\), \(\gamma>0\), and let
\((s_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\) be positive elements of \(A\).
Suppose that \(\mathcal K(x,\gamma)\ne\varnothing\) and that, for
every \(\sigma\in\mathcal K(x,\gamma)\), some
\(\sigma(s_\alpha)\) is nonzero.  Then there are
\(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\) and \(t>0\) such that
\[
 \sigma\in\mathcal K(x,\gamma)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \max_{1\le i\le m}\|\sigma(s_{\alpha_i})\|>t.
\]
Thus the nonvanishing loci of the cuts
\((s_{\alpha_i}-t)_+\) still cover \(\mathcal K(x,\gamma)\).
For a finite covering family of positive contractions, continuous
functional calculus can replace its members by positive contractions
with the same supports and with maximum represented norm equal to one
at every \(\sigma\in\mathcal K(x,\gamma)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Pure-state compression]\label{norm:excision}
Let \(\lambda\) be a pure state of a unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(D\), with
irreducible GNS representation \((\pi,\mathcal H,\xi)\).
Given a finite subset \(\mathcal E\subset D\) and \(\epsilon>0\), there
is a positive contraction \(q\in D\) such that
\[
 \pi(q)\xi=\xi,\qquad
 \|qyq-\lambda(y)q^2\|<\epsilon\quad(y\in\mathcal E).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cuts, placement, and witness bounds]
\label{lem:pre:cut-placement}
Let \(D\) be a \(C^*\)-algebra.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(a,b\in D_+\) and \(\|a-r^*br\|<\epsilon\), then there is
\(v\in D\) with
\[
 v^*v=(a-\epsilon)_+,\qquad vv^*\in\her(b).
\]
Consequently, if \(a\precsim b\), the hereditary algebra of every
positive cut of \(a\) can be placed in \(\her(b)\) by a polar
isometry.
\item If \(a\in\Ideal(b)_+\), then for every \(\epsilon>0\) there is
a finite integer \(L\) such that
\[
 [(a-\epsilon)_+]\le L[b].
\]
If \([a]\le L[b]\), every positive cut of \(a\) still compares to
\(L[(b-\delta)_+]\) for a sufficiently small \(\delta>0\).
\item Comparisons between elements of a hereditary subalgebra can
be witnessed in that subalgebra. Comparisons between specified
matrix corners can be witnessed by the appropriate rectangular
matrices.
\item If \(u\precsim(y-\beta)_+\), where \(0\le\alpha<\beta\), then for
each \(\eta>0\) there is \(r\in D\) such that
\[
 \|u-r^*(y-\alpha)_+r\|<\eta,\qquad
 \|r\|^2\le\frac{\|u\|+\eta}{\beta-\alpha}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Trace transfer]
\label{ext:lem:transfer}
Let $B$ be a simple stable $C^*$-algebra, let $a\in B_+$ be a
contraction, and let $0\ne h\in B_+$. Suppose that
$r:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and vanishes on $[0,\delta]$
for some $0<\delta<1$. There is $c\in\her_B(h)_+$ such that
\[
 \tau(c)=\tau(r(a))
\]
for every lower-semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ on $B$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer between two supports]\label{lem:transfer}
Suppose that $A$ satisfies \textup{(C)}.  Let $B\subseteq A$ be hereditary,
let $D\in M_l(B)_+$ and $E\in B_+$, and suppose that
$w_1,\ldots,w_m\in M_{l,1}(B)$ satisfy
\[
 w_iw_i^*\in\her(D),\qquad w_i^*w_i\in\her(E).
\]
For each $\delta>0$ there is a contraction $v\in M_{l,1}(B)$ such that
\[
 vv^*\in\her(D),\qquad v^*v\in\her(E),
\]
and, in every representation $\sigma$ of $B$,
\[
 \max_{1\le i\le m}\|\sigma(w_i)\|\ge\delta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|\sigma(v)\|=1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison from a uniform rank gap]
\label{lem:G}
Suppose \(A\) is exact and satisfies \eqref{eq:pre:au}. If \(v,w\in A_+\)
satisfy
\[
 d_\tau(v)\le\tfrac12d_\tau(w)
\]
for every lower semicontinuous extended trace on \(A\), then
\(v\precsim w\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Cone placement]
\label{lem:placement}
Assume \eqref{eq:pre:au}--\eqref{eq:pre:div}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let \(B\) be a hereditary subalgebra of a matrix algebra over
\(A\otimes\K\), let \(b\in B_+\) be a contraction, and let \(N\ge1\)
and \(\epsilon>0\). There is a c.p.c.\ order-zero map
\(\psi:M_N\to\her_B(b)\) such that
\[
 \|\sigma(\psi(1))\|=1
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 \sigma((b-\epsilon)_+)\ne0.
\]
Its \(N\) diagonal weights are orthogonal and equivalent in
\(\her_B(b)\). Each diagonal weight, cut at \(1/2\), dominates a
positive class \(u_0\) for which
\[
 [(b-\epsilon)_+]\le(N+1)u_0.
\]
\item Let \(C\) be isomorphic to a finite direct sum of hereditary
subalgebras as above. For \(b\in C_+\) a contraction, \(k\ge1\), and
\(0<q\le1\), there is a c.p.c.\ order-zero map
\(\psi:M_k\to\her_C(b)\), with weight \(t=\psi(1)\), such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:pre:P}
 d_\sigma(t)\le q\,d_\sigma(b),\qquad
 d_\sigma((t-\tfrac12)_+)
       \ge(q/3)d_\sigma((b-\tfrac12)_+)
\end{equation}
for every bounded positive trace \(\sigma\) on \(C\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded diagonalization]
\label{lem:diagonal}
Suppose a countable family of norm-continuous algebraic and
functional-calculus conditions, with fixed coefficients in a norm
ultrapower, is approximately satisfiable on every finite subfamily.
Suppose each unknown has a fixed individual norm bound in these
finite solutions. Then the conditions can be satisfied exactly in
the ultrapower. Additional countably many commutator conditions and
conditions after multiplication by a fixed countable subset of the
algebra may be imposed in the same way.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lipschitz calculus in tracial $2$-norm]\label{tr:lipschitz}
Let $\mathcal M$ be a von Neumann algebra with a finite normal trace $T$,
let $H=H^*\in\mathcal M$, and let $B\in\mathcal M$.  If $f$ is real-valued
and Lipschitz on an interval containing the spectrum of $H$, then
\[
 \|[f(H),B]\|_{2,T}
 \leq\operatorname{Lip}(f)\|[H,B]\|_{2,T}.
\]
Consequently, if $W$ is a finite row, $a=a^*$ and $m=m^*$ are compatible
contractions, and
\[
 R=W(1+W^*W)^{-1/2},
\]
then $\|R\|\leq1$ and
\[
 \|aR-Rm\|_{2,T}\leq\|aW-Wm\|_{2,T}.
\]
The constants do not depend on the size of the matrices or on $\|W\|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian quadratic estimates]\label{lem:gaussian-quadratic}
Let \(W\) be a standard Gaussian vector in a finite-dimensional
real Euclidean space, and let \(B\) be a real symmetric operator
on that space. Put
\[
 q_B=\langle W,BW\rangle-\Tr(B).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:quadratic-variance-characteristic}
 \|q_B\|_{L^2}=\sqrt{2}\,\|B\|_{\HS},
 \qquad
 \bigl|\mathbb E\exp(\iu s q_B)\bigr|
 \leq\bigl(1+4s^2\|B\|_{\HS}^2\bigr)^{-1/4}
 \quad(s\in\R).
\end{equation}
Its law has an exponential moment of its absolute value and is
determined by its moments.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[From moments to bounded continuous functions]\label{lem:quadratic-moment-transfer}
Let \(X_j=X_j^*\) belong to unital \(\mathrm{C}^*\)-algebras
equipped with states \(\varphi_j\). Let \(q_B\) be a centered
Gaussian quadratic as in Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-quadratic}.
Suppose that
\[
 \varphi_j(X_j^d)\longrightarrow\mathbb E(q_B^d)
 \qquad(d=0,1,2,\ldots).
\]
Then, for every bounded continuous function \(f:\R\to\C\),
\[
 \varphi_j(f(X_j))\longrightarrow\mathbb E f(q_B).
\]
No uniform bound on \(\|X_j\|\) is needed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Let \(A\) be a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear,
stably finite complex \(\mathrm C^*\)-algebra satisfying
\(A\cong A\otimes\Zalg\). Let \(G\) be a countable discrete amenable group
and let \(\alpha:G\to\Aut(A)\) be any action. Put
\[
 B=A\otimes\Zalg,\qquad
 \beta_g=\alpha_g\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\Zalg}.
\]
There are a unital \(*\)-isomorphism \(\Phi:A\to B\) and unitaries
\(u_g\in B\), \(g\in G\), such that
\begin{align}
 u_e&=1,& u_{gh}&=u_g\beta_g(u_h),\label{eq:cocycle}\\
 \Phi(\alpha_g(a))&=u_g\beta_g(\Phi(a))u_g^*
 &&(g\in G,\ a\in A).\label{eq:conjugacy}
\end{align}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Szab\'o--Wouters]\label{thm:absorption}
Let a countable discrete amenable group act on a separable, unital,
simple, nuclear, \(\Zalg\)-stable \(\mathrm C^*\)-algebra with
nonempty tracial-state space. If the action has equivariant uniform
property Gamma, it is cocycle conjugate to its tensor product with
the trivial action on \(\Zalg\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Commuting orbit rows]
\label{prop:rows}
There are unital embeddings
\(\iota_i\colon\Zalg\to A^\omega\), \(i\geq 1\), for which the unital
orbit algebras
\[
 C_i=C^*\bigl(\bar\alpha_g(\iota_i(\Zalg)):g\in G\bigr)
\]
commute with \(A\) and commute pairwise. In particular,
\[
 C=C^*\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\geq 1}C_i\Bigr)
 \subseteq A^\omega\cap A'
\]
is unital, separable, and \(\bar\alpha\)-invariant, and
\(\T(C)\neq\varnothing\).

Moreover, there are self-adjoint elements \(x_{i,g}\in C_i\),
\(i\geq 1\), \(g\in G\), and a constant \(M<\infty\), such that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:row-normalization}
 \|x_{i,g}\|\leq M,\qquad
 \varphi(x_{i,g})=0,\qquad
 \varphi(x_{i,g}^2)=1
 \quad\bigl(\varphi\in\T(C)\bigr),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:row-equivariance}
 \bar\alpha_h(x_{i,g})=x_{i,hg}
 \qquad(i\geq1,\ g,h\in G).
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Independence at extreme traces]
\label{lem:factor-independence}
Let \(B\) be a unital \(C^*\)-algebra generated by pairwise commuting
unital \(C^*\)-subalgebras \(B_i\), \(i\geq1\). If
\(\varphi\in\partial_{\mathrm e}\T(B)\), then
\[
 \varphi(b_1\cdots b_s)=\prod_{j=1}^s\varphi(b_j)
\]
whenever \(b_j\in B_{i_j}\) and the indices \(i_1,\ldots,i_s\)
are distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Joint ordered moment limit]
\label{prop:joint-clt}
Let \(J\subseteq G\) be nonempty and finite. Let \(N_j\to\infty\)
be a sequence of positive integers, and let
\(\varphi_j\in\partial_{\mathrm e}\T(C)\). Suppose that
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:covariance-convergence}
 \varphi_j(k_{N_j;g,h})\longrightarrow R_{g,h}
 \qquad(g,h\in J).
\end{equation}
Then \(R=(R_{g,h})_{g,h\in J}\) is a real positive semidefinite
matrix with diagonal entries one.
Choose unit vectors \(v_g\), \(g\in J\), spanning a
finite-dimensional real Euclidean space \(L\), with
\(\langle v_g,v_h\rangle=R_{g,h}\). If \(W\) is a standard
Gaussian vector in \(L\) and
\(\xi_g=\langle v_g,W\rangle\), then
\[
 \bigl((z_{N_j,g})_{g\in J},(k_{N_j;g,h})_{g,h\in J}\bigr)
 \longrightarrow
 \bigl((\xi_g)_{g\in J},(R_{g,h})_{g,h\in J}\bigr)
\]
in all ordered joint moments under \(\varphi_j\).
Equivalently, for every noncommutative \(*\)-polynomial \(P\)
in these self-adjoint variables,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:joint-polynomial-limit}
 \varphi_j\!\left(
 P\bigl((z_{N_j,g})_g,(k_{N_j;g,h})_{g,h}\bigr)\right)
 \longrightarrow
 \mathbb E\,P\bigl((\xi_g)_g,(R_{g,h})_{g,h}\bigr).
\end{equation}
For every sequence \((N_j,\varphi_j)\) as above, a subsequence
satisfying Equation~\eqref{eq:covariance-convergence} exists.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
Let $N\subset M$ be a unital inclusion of von Neumann algebras with separable
preduals, and suppose that there is a faithful normal conditional expectation
$E_N:M\to N$. There exist a unital amenable von Neumann subalgebra $P\subset N$
and a faithful normal conditional expectation $F:N\to P$ such that
\[
 P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M).
\]
Here amenable means injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:masa}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, there is a maximal abelian
subalgebra $A\subset N$ with a faithful normal conditional expectation
$F:N\to A$ such that
\[
 A'\cap c(M)=c(A)\vee\bigl(N'\cap c(M)\bigr).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:products}
The expectations satisfy
\[
 E_N|_B=\varphi(\cdot)1,\qquad E_B|_N=\varphi(\cdot)1.
\]
Consequently the maps
\[
 R(x\Omega\otimes a\Omega)=xa\Omega,\qquad
 L(x\Omega\otimes a\Omega)=ax\Omega
 \qquad(x\in N,\ a\in B)
\]
extend to isometries from $H\otimes K$ to $\HH$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Free position in the full ultrapower]
\label{lem:free-position}
Let \(Q\subset P\) be a unital irreducible inclusion of
\(\mathrm{II}_1\) factors, with \(P\) of separable predual.  For any
nonprincipal ultrafilter \(\omega\) on \(\N\), there is a subfactor
\(D\subset Q^\omega\), generated by increasing unital full matrix
algebras of unbounded sizes, which is free from the constant copy of
\(P\) in the tracial ultrapower \(P^\omega\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Finite standard multiplicities]
\label{prop:finite-copies}
Let \(M\) be a separable-predual \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor, and let
\(M\) act on \(H_r=L^2(M)^r\) by common left multiplication, where
\(r\geq1\) is finite.  For every \(Y\in\mathcal B(H_r)\), every
finite \(h\geq1\), and every \(X\in M_h(M)\),
\[
 \norm{[Y^{(h)},X]}
       \leq (3c_1+2)\,g_M(Y)\,\norm{X}.
\]
Here \(X\) denotes its entrywise action on \(H_r^h\); the constant
is independent of \(M,r,h\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Similarity]\label{thm:similarity}
Let \(A\) be any unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra, let \(H\) be any complex
Hilbert space, and let \(\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)\) be a bounded,
complex-linear, unital algebra homomorphism.  There exists an operator
\(S\in\mathcal B(H)\), invertible with bounded inverse, such that
\[
  \rho(a)=S\pi(a)S^{-1}\qquad(a\in A)
\]
is a \(*\)-homomorphism.  In particular,
\(\rho(a^*)=\rho(a)^*\) for every \(a\in A\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Universal hyperreflexivity]\label{cor:hyperreflexivity}
Let \(H\) be any complex Hilbert space and let
\(M\subset\mathcal B(H)\) be a unital von Neumann algebra. For
\(T\in\mathcal B(H)\), set
\[
 \alpha_M(T)=\sup\{\|(1-e)Te\|:e\in M',\ e=e^*=e^2\}.
\]
Then, with the absolute constant \(C\) from Theorem~\ref{thm:universal},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:universal-hyperreflexivity}
 \dist(T,M)\le 2C\,\alpha_M(T)\qquad(T\in\mathcal B(H)).
\end{equation}
Thus every such \(M\) is hyperreflexive with constant at most \(2C\),
independently of the algebra, its representation, and the Hilbert space.
No optimality of this constant is asserted.
\end{corollary}

\begin{lemma}[Column factorization in a cyclic representation]
\label{lem:cyclic-factorization}
Let \(P\subset\mathcal B(K)\) be a unital von Neumann algebra with a
cyclic vector. For every integer \(h\ge1\) and every unit vector
\(\xi=(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_h)\in K^h\), there are a unit vector
\(\zeta\in K\) and a contraction \(v=(v_i)\in M_{h,1}(P)\) such
that \(\xi_i=v_i\zeta\) for every \(i\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Kirchberg's similarity--derivation equivalence]
\label{thm:kirchberg}
For a unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), the following properties are
equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Every bounded unital homomorphism
 \(\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)\), on any Hilbert space \(H\), is similar
 by a bounded invertible operator to a \(*\)-homomorphism.
 \item For every faithful unital \(*\)-representation
 \(\sigma:A\to\mathcal B(K)\), on any Hilbert space \(K\), every
 bounded linear map \(\Delta:A\to\mathcal B(K)\) satisfying
 \[
  \Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\sigma(b)+\sigma(a)\Delta(b)
 \]
 has the form \(\Delta(a)=V\sigma(a)-\sigma(a)V\) for some
 \(V\in\mathcal B(K)\).
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Symmetrization]\label{lem:free-symmetrization}
In proving Theorem~\ref{thm:free-corner}, one may suppose in addition
that $G$ commutes with $W_u$ for every
$u\in\bigcup_j\mathcal U(D_j)$.  This replacement preserves the
compressed commutator in \eqref{eq:free-corner-conclusion} exactly,
and preserves \eqref{eq:free-corner-hypothesis} for both $G$ and $G^*$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant intertwiners]\label{lem:invariant-intertwiners}
Let $k,l\geq0$, and let
\[
 Y:E\otimes(E^\circ)^{\otimes k}
       \longrightarrow E\otimes(E^\circ)^{\otimes l}
\]
be bounded.  Suppose that $Y$ intertwines the left $D$ actions and
that
\[
 Y C_u^{\otimes(k+1)}=C_u^{\otimes(l+1)}Y
 \qquad(u\in\bigcup_j\mathcal U(D_j)).
\]
Then $Y=0$ if $k\ne l$.  If $k=l$, there are scalars
$(a_\sigma)_{\sigma\in S_k}$ such that
\[
 Y=I_E\otimes\sum_{\sigma\in S_k}a_\sigma U_\sigma,
 \qquad
 U_\sigma(x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_k)
   =x_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}.
\]
For $k=0$ the sum consists of the scalar multiple of the identity
corresponding to the empty permutation.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
There exist $\varepsilon_0>0$, separable complex Hilbert spaces $H_n$,
and von Neumann algebras $M_n,N_n\subseteq\mathcal B(H_n)$ with common
identity $I_{H_n}$ such that
\[
 \gamma(M_n,N_n)\longrightarrow 0,
\]
but, for all sufficiently large $n$, every unitary
$u\in\mathcal B(H_n)$ satisfying $uM_nu^*\subseteq N_n$ obeys
\[
 \|u-I_{H_n}\|\geq\varepsilon_0.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:clock}
For $n\geq3$, let $U_n,V_n$ be the unitaries on $\mathbb C^n$ given by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:clock-shift}
 U_ne_j=\omega_n^je_j,\qquad
 V_ne_j=e_{j+1\bmod n},\qquad
 \omega_n=e^{2\pi i/n}\quad(0\leq j<n).
\end{equation}
Then $\nu_n:=\|U_nV_n-V_nU_n\|=|\omega_n-1|\to0$.
There is no infinite subsequence along which commuting unitaries
$\widehat U_n,\widehat V_n$ on $\mathbb C^n$ satisfy
\[
 \|\widehat U_n-U_n\|+\|\widehat V_n-V_n\|\longrightarrow0.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:corner}
For each $n$, let $E_{1n},E_{2n}$ be commuting projections on a complex
Hilbert space $H_n$, with $D_n=E_nH_n$ nonzero and finite-dimensional,
where $E_n=E_{1n}E_{2n}$. Let $\widetilde R_{1n},\widetilde R_{2n}$
be unitaries commuting with both projections, and write
$R_{in}=\widetilde R_{in}|_{D_n}$.
Suppose $\mathcal A_{1n},\mathcal A_{2n}\subset\B(H_n)$ are
commuting unital von Neumann algebras and there are
$T_{in}\in\mathcal A_{in}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-hypothesis}
 \|T_{in}-E_{in}\widetilde R_{in}\|\longrightarrow0
 \quad(i=1,2).
\end{equation}
Then, for all sufficiently large $n$, there are commuting unitaries
$\widehat R_{1n},\widehat R_{2n}$ on $D_n$ with
\[
 \|\widehat R_{in}-R_{in}\|\longrightarrow0\quad(i=1,2).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp bound after Jiang--Su absorption]
\label{intro:main}
For every separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra $A_0$,
\[
 \nucdim(A_0\otimes\Z)\le1.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Brown--Carri\'on--White]
\label{prelim:bcw}
For every separable nuclear $D$ there are finite-dimensional algebras
$F_n$ and c.p.c. maps
\[
 D\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}D
\]
such that $\beta_n\alpha_n\to\id_D$ in point-norm,
$\|\alpha_n(a)\alpha_n(b)\|\to0$ for orthogonal $a,b\in D_+$, and
each $\beta_n$ is a finite convex combination of c.p.c. order-zero maps
$F_n\to D$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Finite compressions of a full element]
\label{prelim:full-compressions}
If $v\in D_+$ is full and $D$ is unital, then there are
$y_1,\ldots,y_N\in D$ such that
\[
 \sum_{l=1}^N y_l^*vy_l=1_D.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[R\o rdam's comparison criterion]
\label{prelim:comparison}
If $D\cong D\otimes\Z$, then $W(D)$ is almost unperforated.
More generally, if $W(D)$ is almost unperforated, $u,v\in D_+$,
$u\in\Ideal_D(v)$, and
\[
 d([u])<d([v])\quad\text{for every dimension function $d$ with }d([v])=1,
\]
then $u\precsim v$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison with a uniform rank gap]
\label{prelim:half-comparison}
Let $D$ be exact and $\Z$-stable.  If $u,v\in D_+$ satisfy
\[
 d_\tau(u)\le\tfrac12d_\tau(v)
 \quad\text{for every lower semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ on $D$},
\]
then $u\precsim v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Extended traces on finite matrices]
\label{prelim:matrix-traces}
Let $A$ be unital, let $k\ge1$, and let $\lambda$ be a lower
semicontinuous extended trace on $A\otimes M_k$.  Set
$\tau(a)=\lambda(a\otimes1_k)$ and
$L_k=\id_A\otimes\operatorname{tr}_k$, with normalized matrix trace.
Then
\[
 \lambda(z)=\tau(L_k(z))\qquad(z\in(A\otimes M_k)_+).
\]
No finiteness assumption on $\lambda$ is needed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Kirchberg's $\varepsilon$-test]
\label{prelim:epsilon-test}
Let $X_n$ be nonempty sets and let
$f_{j,n}:X_n\to[0,\infty)$ be given for $j,n\in\N$.
Suppose that for every $m$ and $\delta>0$ there is
$(x_n)\in\prod_nX_n$ with
$\lim_{n\to\omega}f_{j,n}(x_n)<\delta$ for $1\le j\le m$.
Then there is a single $(x_n)$ for which all these ultralimits are zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A spare spectral cut gives bounded witnesses]
\label{prelim:bounded-witness}
Let $u,y\in D_+$ and $0\le a<b$.  If
$u\precsim(y-b)_+$, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $r\in D$
such that
\[
 \|u-r^*(y-a)_+r\|<\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \|r\|^2\le\frac{\|u\|+\varepsilon}{b-a}.
\]
Here $(y-0)_+=y$.  In particular the bound is uniform in a family of
contractions $u$ with a common gap $b-a>0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Gabe's approximate domination theorem]
\label{prelim:domination}
Let $D$ be exact and let $\Phi,\Psi:D\to E$ be nuclear completely
positive maps, with $\Psi$ of order zero.  Suppose
\[
 \Phi(a)\in\Ideal_E(\Psi(a))\qquad(a\in D_+).
\]
For every finite $\mathcal F\subset D$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are
$y_1,\ldots,y_N\in E$ such that
\[
 \left\|\Phi(a)-\sum_{l=1}^Ny_l^*\Psi(a)y_l\right\|<\varepsilon
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal F).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Relative-commutant unitary equivalence]
\label{prelim:unitary}
Let $D_n$ be separable unital $\Z$-stable algebras, put
$D_\omega=\prod_\omega D_n$, and let $A$ be separable and unital.
For a c.p.c. order-zero map $\rho:A\to D_\omega$ set
\[
 C=D_\omega\cap\rho(A)'\cap\{1-\rho(1)\}^{\perp}.
\]
Assume that $C$ is full in $D_\omega$ and that every full hereditary
subalgebra $E\subset C$ has the following property:
whenever $x\in E$ admits totally full $e_l,e_r\in E_+$ with
$e_lx=xe_r=0$, there is a full $s\in E$ satisfying $sx=xs=0$.
If $h_0,h_1\in C_+$ are totally full contractions and
\[
 f(h_0)\sim f(h_1)\quad\text{in }C
 \qquad\text{for every }f\in C_0((0,1])_+,
\]
then $uh_1u^*=h_0$ for some unitary $u\in\widetilde C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Matrix model]
 \label{model:construction}
There are finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebras $F_n$, powers $k_n$ of
$2$, and completely positive contractive maps
\[
 A\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n
 \xrightarrow{\beta_n}A\otimes M_{k_n},
 \qquad \theta_n=\beta_n\alpha_n,
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Each $\beta_n$ has order zero, and
 \[
  \|\alpha_n(c)\alpha_n(d)\|\longrightarrow0
  \quad(c,d\in A_+,\ cd=0).
 \]
 \item For every $a\in A$,
 \[
  \|L_{k_n}(\theta_n(a))-a\|\longrightarrow0.
 \]
 \item For every $n,j\geq1$ there is a positive contraction
 $w_{n,j}\in A\otimes M_{k_n}$, and there are nonnegative numbers
 $\eta_{n,j},\delta_{n,j}$ tending to zero as $n\to\infty$ for each
 fixed $j$, such that
 \begin{align}
  \|w_{n,j}-\theta_n(x_j)\|&\leq\eta_{n,j},
       \label{model:retained-norm}\\
  \tau(L_{k_n}(w_{n,j}))
     &\leq \tau(x_j)+\delta_{n,j}d_\tau(b_j)
       \label{model:retained-trace}
 \end{align}
 for every lower semicontinuous extended trace $\tau$ on $A$ with
 $d_\tau(b_j)<\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
The coefficients in \eqref{model:retained-trace} are independent of
$\tau$.  One may take $\delta_{n,j}=2^{-n}$ for all $n,j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Finite-stage model]
 \label{model:finite-stage}
Fix $m\geq1$, a finite subset $\mathcal F$ of the unit ball of $A$,
a finite family $\mathcal O$ of pairs of orthogonal positive
contractions in $A$, and $\varepsilon>0$.  There are a
finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra $F$, a power $k$ of $2$, completely
positive contractive maps
\[
 A\xrightarrow{\alpha}F\xrightarrow{\beta}A\otimes M_k,
 \qquad\theta=\beta\alpha,
\]
and positive contractions $w_1,\ldots,w_m\in A\otimes M_k$ such
that $\beta$ has order zero and
\begin{align}
 \|L_k(\theta(a))-a\|&<\varepsilon
       &&(a\in\mathcal F), \label{model:finite-approx}\\
 \|\alpha(c)\alpha(d)\|&<\varepsilon
       &&((c,d)\in\mathcal O), \label{model:finite-orth}\\
 \|w_j-\theta(x_j)\|&<\varepsilon
       &&(1\leq j\leq m), \label{model:finite-retained}\\
 \tau(L_k(w_j))&\leq\tau(x_j)+\varepsilon d_\tau(b_j)
       &&(1\leq j\leq m, d_\tau(b_j)<\infty).
       \label{model:finite-trace}
\end{align}
The last inequality holds for every lower semicontinuous extended
trace $\tau$ satisfying the indicated finite-rank condition.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{supplies:order-zero}
For every integer $k\geq 1$ and every $\xi>0$ there is a c.p.c.
order-zero map $\iota\colon M_k\to\Z$ such that
\[
 \tau_{\Z}(\iota(1))>1-\xi,
 \qquad \|\iota(e_{11})\|=1.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Localized comparison]\label{trace:comparison}
There is a sequence $m(n)\geq2$ with $m(n)\to_\omega\infty$ such
that, on putting
\[
 P_n=D_{m(n)}\in\Z_2,\qquad P=(P_n)_\omega\in B,
 \qquad
 \Psi(a)=P(q-1/2)_+\pi(a),
\]
the map $\Psi\colon A\to B$ is c.p.c. order zero and, for every
$j\geq1$,
\begin{equation}\label{trace:small-part-comparison}
 e\pi(x_j),\ e\theta(x_j)
 \precsim (\Psi(a_j)-c_j)_+
 \quad\text{in }B,
 \qquad c_j=\gamma_j/64.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}\label{conjugacy:hereditary}
Let $D\subset C$ be a full hereditary subalgebra.  Suppose that
$y\in D$ and that totally full positive elements $e_l,e_r\in D$
satisfy
\[
 e_l y=ye_r=0.
\]
Then there is a full element $s\in D$ with $sy=ys=0$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Two-colour corner approximation]
\label{end:corner}
Let $A$ be a nonzero separable unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra and put
$R=A\otimes\Z^{\otimes3}$. For every finite $\mathcal F\subset A$
and $\varepsilon>0$, the map
\[
 \kappa_A:A\longrightarrow M_2(R),\qquad
 \kappa_A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a\otimes1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
admits a finite-dimensional approximation with two colours:
there are a finite-dimensional algebra $F$, a c.p.c. map
$\alpha:A\to F$, and c.p.c. order-zero maps
$\varphi_0,\varphi_1:F\to M_2(R)$ such that
\[
 \|\varphi_0\alpha(a)+\varphi_1\alpha(a)-\kappa_A(a)\|
 <\varepsilon\qquad(a\in\mathcal F).
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Passing from a corner to the stabilization]
\label{end:stabilize}
Let $A$ be unital. Suppose that the first-corner inclusion
$A\to M_2(A)$ has finite-dimensional approximations with two colours,
with a c.p.c. first map and c.p.c. order-zero return maps.
Then $\nucdim(A\otimes\mathcal K)\le1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:gaussian}
Fix \(k\geq2\) and \(0<r<1\). There are \(n\geq1\) and \(G\in(\R^k)^{\otimes n}\) such that, for every list of pairs of unit vectors \((u_j^0,u_j^1)_{j=1}^n\) satisfying
\[
 |\langle u_j^0,u_j^1\rangle|\leq r\qquad(1\leq j\leq n),
\]
the numbers
\[
 \big\langle G,u_1^{\alpha_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n^{\alpha_n}\big\rangle,
 \qquad \alpha\in\{0,1\}^n,
\]
include a value greater than \(1/2\) and a value less than \(-1/2\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Winter--Zacharias and Robert--Tikuisis]\label{thm:imports}
Let \(A\ne0\) be separable with \(\nucdim A\leq d<\infty\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item If no hereditary subalgebra of \(A\) has a finite-dimensional
irreducible representation, then there are finitely many finite-dimensional
algebras $E_j$, completely positive order-zero maps
$\varphi_j:E_j\to F(A)$, and elements $c_j\in F(A)$ such that every
matrix summand of every $E_j$ has size at least two and
\[
 1_{F(A)}=\sum_jc_j^*\varphi_j(1_{E_j})c_j.
\]
This is the matrix-threshold-two consequence of the covering-number
bound $\operatorname{cov}(F(A))\le(d+1)^2$
\cite[Definition~4.1 and Proposition~4.3]{WZNuclear}.
\item If \(F(A)\) contains two full orthogonal positive elements, then \(A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z\) \cite[Theorem 1.2]{RT}.
\end{enumerate}
Both assertions apply to nonunital \(A\), with the annihilator quotient just defined.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform lists with a prescribed point]\label{lem:uniform-list}
Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff boundary, let $U\subseteq K$ be nonempty
and open, let $\zeta\in K$, and let $0<\beta<1$.  There is a finite
nonempty list $s_1,\ldots,s_M\in G$, with repetitions allowed, such that
\[
 s_j^{-1}\zeta\in U\quad(1\leq j\leq M),
 \qquad
 \frac{1}{M}\#\{j:s_j^{-1}t\notin U\}<\beta
 \quad(t\in K).
\]
Moreover, some open neighborhood $O$ of $\zeta$ satisfies
$s_j^{-1}O\subseteq U$ for every $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Compatible sparse flags]\label{prop:flags}
Let $G$ be a nonamenable discrete group.  For every integer $N\geq1$
and every $0<\beta<1$, there are finite nonempty sets
$\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_N$ and
$\mathcal Y_0,\ldots,\mathcal Y_{N-1}$, maps
\[
 s_k:\mathcal X_k\times\mathcal Y_{k-1}\longrightarrow G,
 \qquad
 b_k:G\times\mathcal X_k\times\mathcal Y_{k-1}
       \longrightarrow\{\E,\F\},
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(F1)}] If $k<N$ and $b_k(w;x,y)=\E$, then, with
$v=w s_k(x,y)$,
\[
 b_{k+1}(v;x',y')=\E
 \quad\text{for every }(x',y')\in
            \mathcal X_{k+1}\times\mathcal Y_k.
\]
\item[\textup{(F2)}] For every $k,w,x$,
\[
 \frac{\#\{y\in\mathcal Y_{k-1}:b_k(w;x,y)=\F\}}
      {|\mathcal Y_{k-1}|}\leq\beta.
\]
\item[\textup{(F3)}] For every $k,v,y$,
\[
 \frac{\#\{x\in\mathcal X_k:
          b_k(v s_k(x,y)^{-1};x,y)=\E\}}
      {|\mathcal X_k|}\leq\beta.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Each alphabet may subsequently be replaced by any positive integer
number of copies, independently of the others, while preserving these
properties.  In particular, its cardinality can be made arbitrarily
large and divisible by any prescribed positive integer.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer with a prescribed subspace]\label{lem:priority}
Let $A,B$ be positive operators on a Hilbert space $E$ such that
\[
 \tfrac12\id\leq A,B\leq2\id,
 \qquad A-B=h\Gamma,
 \qquad \Gamma^*=\Gamma,
 \qquad \norm{\Gamma}\leq1,
 \qquad 0\leq h\leq\tfrac18.
\]
Let $P$ be an orthogonal projection commuting with $B$, set $R=PE$, and
assume $\norm{P\Gamma P}\leq\eta$, where $0\leq\eta\leq1$.
There is a specified invertible operator $S_R$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:priority-estimates}
 S_R^*AS_R=B,\qquad S_R(R)=R,\qquad
 \norm{S_R-\id}\leq Ch,\qquad
 \norm{(S_R-\id)P}\leq Ch\eta.
\end{equation}
The constant $C$ is absolute, and the estimates also hold in the
$B$-norm after changing $C$.

If $R\subseteq R'$ and both projections satisfy these hypotheses, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nested-transfer}
 K=S_{R'}^{-1}S_R
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 K^*BK=B,\qquad \norm{K-\id}_B\leq Ch,\qquad
 \norm{(K-\id)P}_B\leq Ch\eta.
\end{equation}
The construction commutes with orthogonal direct sums and with every
orthogonal projection commuting with $A$, $B$, and $P$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fixing a subspace exactly]\label{lem:truncate}
Let $U$ be a unitary on a Hilbert space $E$, and let $P$ be an orthogonal
projection.  Suppose
\[
 \norm{U-\id}\leq t<\tfrac12,
 \qquad \norm{(U-\id)P}\leq e\leq\tfrac12.
\]
There is a unitary $\widehat U$ that is the identity on $PE$ and leaves
$(\id-P)E$ invariant, with
\[
 \norm{\widehat U-U}\leq3e,
 \qquad \norm{\widehat U-\id}\leq t+3e.
\]
The statement holds in arbitrary Hilbert space dimension.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:witness}
Let $\rho:G\to\U(H)$ be a unitary representation, and define unit vectors
in $\mathbb C^{\cI}\otimes H$ by
\[
 \psi=\abs{\cI}^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\cI}e_i\otimes\rho(s_i)u_i,
 \qquad
 r=\abs{\cI}^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\cI}e_i\otimes r_i.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:witness-values}
 \ip{\psi}{(D\otimes I)\psi}=0,
 \qquad \ip{r}{(D\otimes I)r}=\frac12.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\norm{r-\psi}\ge1/4$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Induction from a subgroup]\label{lem:subgroup-induction}
Let \(H\) be a subgroup of a discrete group \(G\), and let
\(\sigma:H\to\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal K)\) be a uniformly bounded
representation on a complex Hilbert space. There is a uniformly bounded
representation \(\Pi:G\to\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal L)\) on
\(\mathcal L=\ell^2(G/H;\mathcal K)\) such that
\[
 |\Pi|=|\sigma|.
\]
If \(\Pi\) is unitarizable, then \(\sigma\) is unitarizable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:main}
A discrete group is amenable if and only if it is unitarizable.
For every discrete nonamenable group \(G\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
there are a complex Hilbert space \(\mathcal K\) and a representation
\(\pi:G\to\mathrm{GL}(\mathcal K)\) with \(|\pi|\le1+\varepsilon\)
that is not similar to a unitary representation. If \(G\) is countable,
\(\mathcal K\) may be chosen separable.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Distance from the translation commutant]
\label{lem:kernel-obstruction}
Let $G$ be a countable group, let $k$ be a positive integer, and let
$A,T\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_k)$ with $A\in U_k(G)'$.
Write
\[
  A[x,y]=W(x^{-1}y),\qquad
  E=\sum_{s\in G}\norm{W(s)}_{\HS}^2.
\]
Suppose that, for some $K\ge0$,
\[
  \norm{\operatorname{row}_e(T)}\le K,
  \qquad
  \norm{\operatorname{col}_e(A-T)}\le K.
\]
Then $E$ is finite and, for every $C\in U_k(G)'$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kernel-energy-obstruction}
  E\le 4k\bigl(K+\norm{T-C}\bigr)^2.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:kernel-distance-obstruction}
  \dist\bigl(T,U_k(G)'\bigr)
  \ge \frac12\sqrt{\frac{E}{k}}-K,
\end{equation}
where $\dist(T,U_k(G)')=\inf_{C\in U_k(G)'}\norm{T-C}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Direct-sum obstruction]
\label{prop:direct-sum-obstruction}
Let $G$ be a countable group.
For each $j\in\N$, let $k_j$ be a positive integer, put
\[
  \mathcal H_j=\ell^2(G;\C^{k_j}),
  \qquad (U_j(g)\xi)(x)=\xi(g^{-1}x),
\]
and let $A_j,T_j\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H_j)$ with
$A_j\in U_j(G)'$.
Write
\[
  A_j[x,y]=W_j(x^{-1}y),\qquad
  E_j=\sum_{s\in G}\norm{W_j(s)}_{\HS}^2.
\]
Suppose that one constant $K\ge0$ satisfies
\begin{align*}
  \norm{\operatorname{row}_e(T_j)}&\le K, &
  \norm{\operatorname{col}_e(A_j-T_j)}&\le K
  &&(j\in\N),\\
  \norm{T_j-U_j(g)T_jU_j(g)^{-1}}&\le K
  &&&&(j\in\N,\ g\in G).
\end{align*}
Assume also that
\[
  \frac{E_j}{k_j}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Then $G$ has a representation on a separable complex Hilbert space
whose operators are bounded and invertible, with
\[
  \sup_{g\in G}\norm{\pi(g)}\le1+K,
\]
and which is not similar to a unitary representation.
No uniform bound on $\norm{T_j}$ or $\norm{A_j}$ is assumed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:contracting-average}
If \(G\) is a nonamenable discrete group, there are a finite set
\(S\subset G\) containing \(e\), with \(d=|S|\ge2\), and a number
\(0<\rho<1\) such that
\[
 \norm{\frac1d\sum_{t\in S}R_t}\le\rho.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[An upper bound for all small subfamilies]
\label{lem:frames}
Let $n\ge 2$ and $r\ge 1$ be integers, and put
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:frame-parameters}
 p=\min(2r,n),\qquad
 k=\left\lceil 2r\log(2n)\right\rceil,
 \qquad b_0=10,
\end{equation}
where $\log$ denotes the natural logarithm.  There are unit vectors
$v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\C^k$ such that, for every
$J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|J|\le p$, the operator
\[
 V_J\colon\ell^2(J)\longrightarrow\C^k,
 \qquad V_J z=\sum_{i\in J}z_i v_i,
\]
satisfies $\norm{V_J}\le b_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The masked operator estimate]
\label{lem:masked}
In the preceding setting, let $1\le p\le n$ and $b_0>0$.  Suppose
that
\[
 \norm{V_J}\le b_0
 \quad\text{for every }J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}
 \text{ with }|J|\le p,
\]
where $V_J$ is the synthesis operator with columns $v_i$, $i\in J$.
For a mask $c$ as in \Cref{eq:masked-operator}, define
\[
 \mathcal R_x=\{i:c(x,i)\ne0\},\qquad
 \mathcal C_y=\{i:c(ys_i^{-1},i)\ne0\}.
\]
If $|\mathcal R_x|\le p$ for every $x\in G$ and $|\mathcal C_y|\le p$ for every
$y\in G$, then
\[
 \norm{T_c}\le b_0^2.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{corollary}[Individual block rows and columns]
\label{cor:block-rows-columns}
Under \Cref{eq:weights-orientation-bounds}, one has
\[
 \norm{q_xT}\le b_0^2\quad(x\in G),
 \qquad
 \norm{(A-T)\iota_y}\le b_0^2\quad(y\in G).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Strong Kadison--Kastler stability]\label{thm:main}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $\delta=\delta(\eps)>0$ such that the
following holds. If $H$ is any complex Hilbert space and
$M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ are unital von Neumann algebras with identity
$I_H$ and $d(M,N)<\delta$, there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfying
\[
 uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}<\eps.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Amenable near inclusions]\label{thm:amenable}
Let $R,Q\subseteq\B(H)$ be von Neumann algebras with identity $I$, with
$R$ amenable. If $R\subset_\gamma Q$ and $\gamma<1/100$, there is a
unitary $v\in(R\cup Q)''$ such that
\[
 vRv^*\subseteq Q,\qquad \norm{v-I}\le150\gamma.
\]
If also $Q\subset_\gamma R$ and $\gamma<1/101$, the same conclusion
holds with $vRv^*=Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Close representations]\label{lem:paired}
Let $\rho,\theta:P\to\B(H)$ be normal unital $*$-representations of a
von Neumann algebra. If $\norm{\rho-\theta}_{\cb}\le e<1/4$, there
is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ with
\[
 u\rho(x)u^*=\theta(x)\quad(x\in P),\qquad \norm{u-I}\le4e.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[UCP criterion]\label{prop:ucp}
Let $P,Q$ be von Neumann algebras, let
$\rho:P\to\B(H)$ be a faithful normal unital representation, and let
$Q\subseteq\B(H)$ have the same identity. Suppose that $F:P\to Q$ is
UCP and
\[
 \norm{F-\rho}_{\cb}\le e<10^{-3},\qquad
 \sup_{y\in Q_1}\dist(y,\rho(P)_1)\le g,\qquad g+e<1.
\]
Then there is a normal unital $*$-isomorphism $\theta:P\to Q$ and a
unitary $u\in\B(H)$ such that
\[
 \norm{\theta-\rho}_{\cb}\le32e,\qquad
 u\rho(x)u^*=\theta(x)\ (x\in P),\qquad \norm{u-I}\le128e.
\]
The map $F$ need not be normal.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:tensor-gap}
Let $A,B\subseteq\B(H)$ be unital von Neumann algebras with
$\dcb(A,B)\le\gamma$. If $K$ is separable, then
\[
 \dcb(A\barotimes\B(K),B\barotimes\B(K))\le\gamma.
\]
If $D\subseteq\B(K)$ is a von Neumann algebra whose commutant is the
strong closure of increasing finite-dimensional unital algebras, then
\[
 \dcb(A\barotimes D,B\barotimes D)\le\gamma.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariant operator means]\label{lem:invariant-mean}
Let $G$ be a discrete amenable group and $m$ a left invariant mean on
$\ell^\infty(G)$: thus $m$ is a positive unital linear functional with
$m(f(h^{-1}\,\cdot))=m(f)$ for every $h\in G$.
For a bounded family $T_g\in\B(K)$, define
\[
 \ip{(m_gT_g)\xi}{\eta}=m_g\ip{T_g\xi}{\eta}.
\]
This averaging map from bounded operator families to $\B(K)$ is UCP,
commutes with multiplication on either side by a fixed operator, and
preserves weak-operator closed linear subspaces. If
$\norm{T_g-T}\le a$ for every $g$, then
$\norm{m_gT_g-T}\le a$, also at rectangular matrix levels.
No measurability of the family is required.

For a unitary representation $g\mapsto V_g$ on $K$, the map
\[
 E_V(T)=m_gV_gTV_g^*\qquad(T\in\B(K))
\]
is a UCP projection onto $\{V_g:g\in G\}'$. It preserves every von
Neumann algebra invariant under these conjugations.
More generally, for an action by automorphisms $\alpha_g$ on a von
Neumann algebra $P$, the formula
\[
 \varphi(E(x))=m_g\varphi(\alpha_g(x))\qquad(\varphi\in P_*)
\]
defines a UCP map onto $P^G$ fixing that algebra. These averaging maps
need not be normal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform amplification]\label{thm:amplification}
There is an absolute constant \(C_{\mathrm{amp}}\) such that, for every
type \(\II_1\) factor \(M\subseteq\B(H)\) on a separable Hilbert space and
every selfadjoint \(h\in\B(H)\),
\[
 \norm{\ad_h|_M}_{\cb}\le
 C_{\mathrm{amp}}\norm{\ad_h|_M}.
\]
The constant is independent of \(M\), its representation, and \(H\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer from the trace to a normal representation]
\label{lem:trace-transfer}
Let \(P\subseteq\B(K)\) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful
normal trace \(\tau\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \((x_j)\) is bounded and
\(\lim_{j\to\omega}\norm{x_j}_2=0\), then
\(\lim_{j\to\omega}\norm{x_j\xi}=0\) for every \(\xi\in K\).
\item If \(x=(x_j)_\omega\in P^\omega\), then the weak-operator
ultralimit of \(x_j\) in this representation is \(E_P(x)\), where
\(E_P:P^\omega\to P\) is the trace-preserving conditional expectation.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Free projection words]\label{lem:free-words}
For every integer $r\geq 1$ there are constants $C_r>0$ and an integer
$d_r\geq r$ with the following property.  Let $d\geq d_r$, and let
$(\mathcal A,\tau)$ be a von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal
tracial state.  Suppose that $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subset\mathcal A$ are
unital copies of $M_d(\C)$ which are scalar free: the trace of a product
of centered letters from successively different copies is zero.
For each $j$, let $(e_a^{(j)})_{a=1}^d$ be the diagonal minimal
projections of $A_j$.

For a multiset $W$ of cardinality $r$ drawn from $\{1,\ldots,d\}$, put
\[
 B_W=\sum_{\substack{(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}^r\\
                     \text{with multiset }W}}
       e_{a_r}^{(r)}\cdots e_{a_1}^{(1)}.
\]
Then $\norm{B_W}\leq\beta_W$, where
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fw-beta}
 \beta_W=
 \begin{cases}
  7\sqrt{(r-1)!}\,d^{-(r-1)/2},
       &\text{if all labels in $W$ are distinct},\\
  C_r d^{-(r-1)/2},&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
The constants and threshold depend only on $r$, not on the ambient
algebra, the free copies, or $W$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Free Haar unitaries with matrix-algebra lifts]
\label{lem:free-lifts}
Let $M\subseteq\B(H)$ be a separably acting $\II_1$ factor, let
$n\geq1$, and put $P=M_n(M)$.  For every free ultrafilter $\omega$
there is a Haar unitary $s\in P^\omega$ such that $W^*(s)$ and the
constant copy of $P$ are scalar free.  Moreover, $s$ has unitary
representatives
\[
 s=(s_j)_\omega,\qquad
 s_j\in\U(M_n(R_j)),
\]
where each $R_j\subseteq M$ is a unital full matrix algebra.
Consequently, for every $h=h^*\in\B(H)$, with
$\delta=\norm{\ad_h|_M}$ and $h_n=I_n\otimes h$, these representatives
satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:free-lift-commutator}
 \norm{[h_n,s_j]}\leq2\delta\qquad(j\geq1).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Unitary twists of a free Haar unitary]
\label{lem:haar-twist}
Let $(F,\tau)$ be a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, let
$P\subseteq F$ be a unital von Neumann subalgebra, and let $s\in F$
be Haar and scalar free from $P$.  For every $U\in\U(P)$, both
$sU$ and $Us$ are Haar and scalar free from $P$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Equivariant boundary means]\label{lem:boundary-mean}
For every countable group $G$ there are a standard probability space
$(D,\nu)$ with a nonsingular $G$-action and a positive unital contraction
\[
 m:L^\infty(G\times D)\longrightarrow L^\infty(D)
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-mean-identities}
 m(\lambda_g F)=\alpha_g(mF),\qquad m(fF)=f\,m(F)
 \quad(f\in L^\infty(D)).
\end{equation}
There is a mean $m^{(2)}$ with the same properties for the separate
$G\times G$-action on $D\times D$ and functions on
$G^2\times D^2$.  Each mean extends to a contraction on bounded operator
fields on any separable $K$.  The extension preserves adjoints and
von Neumann algebra values, and is a bimodule map over bounded operator
fields independent of the group variable:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-operator-module}
 m(BFC)=B\,m(F)\,C.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Correction of a measurable unitary cocycle]
\label{lem:boundary-correction}
Let $D$ and $m$ be as in \Cref{lem:boundary-mean}, and let
$A\subset\B(K)$ be a von Neumann algebra on a separable Hilbert space.
Suppose $V_g\in L^\infty(D,\U(A))$, $g\in G$, and
\[
 e=\sup_{g,h\in G}\norm{V_g\alpha_g(V_h)-V_{gh}}_\infty
 \le\frac1{64}.
\]
Then there are measurable unitary fields $W_g$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-exact-cocycle}
 W_g\alpha_g(W_h)=W_{gh},\qquad
 \sup_g\norm{W_g-V_g}_\infty\le 2e.
\end{equation}
In particular $W_1=I$.  The identities hold simultaneously almost
everywhere for every $g,h$, and may be used on a $G$-invariant conull
subset of $D$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Averaged intertwiner]\label{lem:boundary-intertwiner}
Take either $(\Gamma,Z)=(G,D)$ or
$(\Gamma,Z)=(G^2,D^2)$, with its mean from
\Cref{lem:boundary-mean}.  Let $U:\Gamma\to\U(K)$ be a unitary
representation on a separable Hilbert space, and let
$\Sigma_s\in L^\infty(Z,\U(K))$ be an exact cocycle for the given
action.  If
\[
 \sup_{s\in\Gamma}\norm{\Sigma_s-U_s}_\infty\le\delta<1,
\]
there is $L\in L^\infty(Z,\U(K))$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-intertwiner}
 \norm{L-I}_\infty\le2\delta,\qquad
 L(z)U_s=\Sigma_s(z)L(s^{-1}z).
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Diagonal comparison in a finite algebra]
\label{lem:boundary-diagonal-unitary}
Let $A$ be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial
state $\tau$ and separable trace Hilbert space $L^2(A,\tau)$.
Let $W_g\in L^\infty(D,\U(A))$ be an exact cocycle.  Suppose
\[
 \sup_{g\in G}\mathop{\rm ess\,sup}_{x,y\in D}
 \norm{W_g(x)W_g(y)^*-I}\le r<1.
\]
Then there is a measurable field $a:D^2\to\U(A)$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-diagonal-unitary}
 \norm{a-I}_\infty\le2r,\qquad
 a(x,y)=W_g(x)a(g^{-1}x,g^{-1}y)W_g(y)^*.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $\sup_g\norm{W_g-u_g}_\infty\le\delta$ for any
constant unitaries $u_g$ on a common representation space, the conclusion
holds with $\norm{a-I}_\infty\le4\delta$ when $2\delta<1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Double ergodicity with unitary coefficients]
\label{lem:double-ergodicity}
For the space $D$ constructed in \Cref{lem:boundary-mean}, let
$\sigma:G\to\U(K)$ be a unitary representation on a separable Hilbert
space.  If a bounded measurable map $f_0:D^2\to K$ satisfies
\[
 f_0(gx,gy)=\sigma(g)f_0(x,y)\quad(g\in G)
\]
almost everywhere, then $f_0$ is almost everywhere a constant vector
fixed by every $\sigma(g)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform stability of finite factors]
\label{thm:finite}
There are a number $t_{\mathrm{fin}}>0$ and a nondecreasing function
$\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}:(0,t_{\mathrm{fin}})\to(0,\infty)$, with
$\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, having the following
property.  Let $H$ be a separable nonzero Hilbert space, let
$M\subseteq\B(H)$ be a unital finite factor, and let $N\subseteq\B(H)$
be a von Neumann algebra with the same identity.  If $d(M,N)<t<t_{\mathrm{fin}}$,
then $N$ is a finite factor and there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ such that
\[
 uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}\le\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}(t).
\]
The threshold and function are independent of $M,N$ and their representations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Increasing matrix algebras with scalar relative commutant]
\label{lem:irreducible-hyperfinite}
Every separable-predual $\II_1$ factor $M$ contains an irreducible unital
hyperfinite $\II_1$ subfactor $R$.  One can write
$R=(\bigcup_j Q_j)''$, where $Q_j$ are increasing unital full matrix
algebras and their sizes tend to infinity.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Common-position theorem]
\label{prop:finite-common-position}
Let $M,N$ be separable-predual $\II_1$ factors acting nondegenerately on
one Hilbert space, with mutual strict $g$-near inclusions, where
$0<g<1.74\cdot10^{-13}$.  Suppose that an amenable von Neumann subalgebra
$R\subseteq M\cap N$ satisfies $R'\cap M\subseteq R$.  There are
faithful normal representations $\pi:M\to\B(K)$ and
$\rho:N\to\B(K)$, a common unit vector $\Omega$, and a number
$\beta<50948\sqrt g$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item both images are in standard tracial position with vector $\Omega$;
\item $\pi|_R=\rho|_R$, and the images have mutual strict
$\beta$-near inclusions;
\item for original contractions $x\in M$, $y\in N$,
\[
 \norm{\pi(x)-\rho(y)}\le\beta+\norm{x-y};
\]
\item if $e_R$ is the projection onto $\overline{\pi(R)\Omega}$,
then $(\pi(M)\cup\{e_R\})''=(\rho(N)\cup\{e_R\})''$.
\end{enumerate}
The space $K$ can be taken separable.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[The common right action]
\label{lem:finite-right-action}
In the setting of \Cref{prop:finite-common-position}, the right actions
of $R$ agree elementwise:
\[
 J_M rJ_M=J_N rJ_N\qquad(r\in R).
\]
In particular $T=J_NJ_M-I$ commutes with the left and right actions of $R$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm control of tracial conjugations]
\label{lem:tracial-conjugations}
Let $M,N\subseteq\B(K)$ be $\II_1$ factors in common standard tracial
position with vector $\Omega$.  Suppose that $R\subseteq M\cap N$ is
an irreducible hyperfinite subfactor of $M$, presented by increasing
matrix algebras, and that its right actions agree.  If $d(M,N)<b$, then
\[
 \norm{J_M-J_N}\le C_Jb,\qquad C_J=768.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:finite-standard-isomorphism}
There are absolute constants $b_0>0$ and $C_{\mathrm{st}}>0$ such that
the following holds. Let $M,N\subseteq\B(K)$ be type $\II_1$ factors
on a separable Hilbert space in common standard tracial position with
vector $\Omega$. Suppose they contain a common hyperfinite $\II_1$
subfactor $R$, irreducible in $M$ and generated by increasing matrix
algebras, and that $J_MrJ_M=J_NrJ_N$ for every $r\in R$.
If $d(M,N)<b<b_0$, then there is
a normal unital star-isomorphism $\vartheta:M\to N$ satisfying
\[
 \sup_{x\in M_1}\norm{\vartheta(x)-x}\le C_{\mathrm{st}}b.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[The fixed tensor factor]
\label{lem:fixed-tensor-factor}
One has $D_\rho'\cap D=\C1$.  If $A$ is any factor with separable predual,
then $A\barotimes D$ is a type $\III_1$ factor and
\[
 A\barotimes D\cong(A\barotimes D)\barotimes R_\lambda,
\]
where $R_\lambda$ is the Powers factor obtained using only
$(M_2(\C),\rho_\lambda)$ sites.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Preparing an infinite pair]
\label{prop:prepared-pair}
There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ with the following property.
Suppose $M_0,N_0\subseteq\B(H)$ are factors on a separable
Hilbert space, $M_0$ is infinite, and $d(M_0,N_0)<t<c$.
For the fixed $D\subseteq\B(K)$
above, there are unitaries $u_0\in\B(H)$ and
$v\in\B(H\otimes K)$ satisfying
\[
 \norm{u_0-1}+\norm{v-1}\leq Ct
\]
such that
\[
 M=M_0\barotimes D,\qquad
 N=v\bigl((u_0N_0u_0^*)\barotimes D\bigr)v^*
\]
form a prepared pair and $\dcb(M,N)\leq Ct$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Uniform graph comparison]
\label{prop:modular-graphs}
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that every prepared pair with
$\dcb(M,N)\leq\gamma$ satisfies
\[
 \sup_{c>0}\norm{E_c^M-E_c^N}\leq C\gamma.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[Logarithmic modular cuts]
\label{cor:modular-cuts}
For a prepared pair with $\dcb(M,N)\leq\gamma$, put
$L_P=\log\Delta_P$, $P=M,N$.  There is an absolute constant $C$ such
that, for every $a\in\R$,
\[
 \norm{1_{(-\infty,a-1/2]}(L_N)
        1_{[a+1/2,\infty)}(L_M)}\leq C\gamma.
\]
The same estimate holds with $M,N$ interchanged.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[A common modular action]
\label{prop:modular-alignment}
There are absolute constants $c_{\rm mod},C_{\rm mod}>0$ with the
following property. Let $(M,N,\Omega,R)$ be a prepared pair as in
\Cref{def:prepared-pair}, acting on the same separable Hilbert space
$H$, and suppose that $\dcb(M,N)<\gamma<c_{\rm mod}$.
There is a unitary $q\in\B(H)$ such that
\[
 \norm{q-I}\le C_{\rm mod}\gamma,
 \qquad \dcb(qMq^*,N)\le C_{\rm mod}\gamma,
 \qquad
 \Delta_N^{it}(qMq^*)\Delta_N^{-it}=qMq^*
 \quad(t\in\R).
\]
The algebra $N$ and its modular group are unchanged.
\end{proposition}

\begin{lemma}[A path of approximate normalizers]
\label{lem:local-normalizer-path}
There are absolute constants $e_0,C_{\rm path}>0$ such that the
following holds. Let $P\subset\B(H)$ be a separably acting type
$\III$ factor,
let $I\subset\R$ be an interval containing $0$, and let
$v:I\to\U(\B(H))$ be norm continuous with $v(0)=I$.
If $0\le e<e_0$ and
\[
 \sup_{t\in I}\sup_{x\in P_1}\dist(v(t)xv(t)^*,P)\le e,
\]
then
\[
 \sup_{t\in I}\dist(v(t),\mathcal G_P)\le C_{\rm path}e.
\]
The constants are independent of the interval's length.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[From modular cuts to near normalizers]
\label{lem:modular-near-normalizers}
Let $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ be a prepared pair on a separable Hilbert space,
with $M$ of type $\III$ and $\dcb(M,N)\leq\gamma$.  Write
\[
 U_P(t)=e^{itL_P},\qquad L_P=\log\Delta_P\quad(P=M,N),
 \qquad W(t)=U_N(t)U_M(t)^*.
\]
Assume the separated-cut estimate of \Cref{cor:modular-cuts}, with its
universal constant, and the local path estimate of
\Cref{lem:local-normalizer-path}.  There are universal constants
$\gamma_0>0$ and $C$ such that, if $0<\gamma<\gamma_0$, then for every
$t\in\R$ there is a unitary $n_t$ satisfying
\[
 n_tMn_t^*=M,\qquad \norm{n_t-W(t)}\leq C\gamma.
\]
No regularity of the choices $t\mapsto n_t$ is asserted or needed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Small exact normalizers]
\label{lem:small-exact-normalizer}
There are absolute $r_0,C_0>0$ such that, if $P$ is a separably
acting type $\III$ factor, $v\in\mathcal N_P$, and
$\norm{v-I}<r_0$, then
\[
 v=ab',\qquad a\in\U(P),\quad b'\in\U(P'),
 \qquad \norm{a-I}+\norm{b'-I}\le C_0\norm{v-I}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Correction of normalizer representations]
\label{lem:normalizer-representation-correction}
There are absolute $e_1,C_1>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $P\subset\B(H)$ be a separably acting type $\III$ factor.
For any family $v_t\in\mathcal N_P$, $t\in\R$, with
\[
 e:=\sup_{t,s\in\R}\norm{v_tv_s-v_{t+s}}<e_1,
\]
there is an exact unitary representation $z:\R\to\mathcal N_P$
of the discrete group with
\[
 \sup_t\norm{z_t-v_t}\le C_1e.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completely bounded gap of common crossed products]
\label{lem:core-gap}
Let $P,Q\subseteq\B(H)$ be normalized by the same group $U$.
If $\dcb(P,Q)<\gamma$, then
\[
 \dcb(C(P,U),C(Q,U))\le\gamma.
\]
The conclusion holds with any strict upper bound in place of $\gamma$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proposition}[Conjugacy through a common crossed product]
\label{prop:core-descent}
There are an absolute $\gamma_0>0$ and a nondecreasing function
$\zeta:(0,\gamma_0)\to(0,\infty)$, with $\zeta(\gamma)\to0$ as
$\gamma\downarrow0$, with the following property.  Suppose
$P,Q\subseteq\B(H)$ are unital von Neumann algebras on a separable
Hilbert space, $\dcb(P,Q)<\gamma<\gamma_0$, and a strongly continuous
unitary group $U$ normalizes both.  If $C(Q,U)$ is a type
$\II_\infty$ factor, then a unitary $a\in\B(H)$ satisfies
\[
 aPa^*=Q,\qquad \norm{a-I}\le\zeta(\gamma).
\]
No factoriality or modular interpretation of $C(P,U)$ is assumed.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform stability of separably acting factors]
\label{thm:factors}
There are an absolute $t_{\rm fac}>0$ and a nondecreasing function
$\eta_{\rm fac}:(0,t_{\rm fac})\to(0,\infty)$ with
$\eta_{\rm fac}(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$ such that the following
holds.  For every separable complex Hilbert space $H$ and every pair
of unital factors $M_0,N_0\subseteq\B(H)$ with the same identity and
$d(M_0,N_0)<t<t_{\rm fac}$, there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ with
\[
 uM_0u^*=N_0,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}\le\eta_{\rm fac}(t).
\]
The function and the threshold are independent of the factors, their
types, and their representations.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:centers-close}
For unital von Neumann algebras $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$,
\[
 d\bigl(Z(M),Z(N)\bigr)\leq 3d(M,N).
\]
Consequently, whenever $d(M,N)<g<1/303$, there is a unitary
$w\in\B(H)$ such that
\[
 wZ(M)w^*=Z(N),\qquad \norm{w-I}\leq450g.
\]
For $N_0=w^*Nw$ one then has $Z(N_0)=Z(M)$ and
$d(M,N_0)<901g$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:fiber-gap}
Let $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ act on a separable Hilbert space and have the
same center.  In their common central decomposition,
\[
 d(M_t,N_t)\leq d(M,N)
 \quad\text{for almost every }t.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:measurable-implementers}
In the setting of \Cref{lem:fiber-gap}, suppose that for some $a>0$
and almost every $t$ there is a unitary $v_t\in\B(H_t)$ satisfying
\[
 v_t M_t v_t^*=N_t,\qquad\norm{v_t-I}<a.
\]
Then there is a unitary $v\in\B(H)$ such that
$vMv^*=N$ and $\norm{v-I}\leq a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:separable-algebras}
For every $a>0$ there is $\delta_{\mathrm{sep}}(a)>0$ such that
whenever $M,N$ are unital von Neumann algebras on a separable Hilbert
space and $d(M,N)<\delta_{\mathrm{sep}}(a)$, there is a unitary $u$
with
\[
 uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I}<a.
\]
The tolerance is independent of the algebras and the representation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:uniform-matrix-commutant}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $\delta>0$, independent of the algebras,
their representations, and their Hilbert spaces, such that unital von
Neumann algebras $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ with the same identity and
$d(M,N)<\delta$ satisfy
\[
 \dcb(M,N)<\eps,\qquad d(M',N')<\eps.
\]
\end{corollary}
